proof_nl: Let x be any real number. By definition, floor(x) is the greatest integer less than or equal to x. Therefore floor(x) is itself less than or equal to x. Since x was arbitrary, this holds for every real number x.
solver_summary: Immediate from the definition of the floor function as the greatest integer not exceeding x.
vetter_reason: The proof directly establishes floor(x) ≤ x from the defining property of the floor function, then universalizes over arbitrary real x. It matches the lemma statement exactly and uses no problematic dependencies.
